scope: Theorem 10.1 (Encoded-path geometry) of the manuscript “The PCP-for-PPAD conjecture: a quasilinear reduction” (preprints/The-PCP-for-PPAD-conjecture-a-quasilinear-reduction-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 136 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a7ab4d86183890be), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 113. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under these hypotheses, there is a union L ⊂ B of directed, rounded paths and cycles, with desired endpoint set E, having the following properties. For every sufficiently small positive rational τ, there are a positive integer B1 and positive rational constants c∗, β0, depending only on d∗ and τ, and a field v : B → R4m such that ∥v(X)∥∞ ≤ B1 − 1, (10.3) ∥clipB(X + βv(X)) − X∥ ≥ c∗β if dist(X, E) > 10τ, 0 < β ≤ β0. (10.4) The field is continuous on the relative open set {X ∈ B : dist(X, E) > 10τ}. Every P ∈ E has first block exactly Ew for a desired endpoint w. Consequently, if ∥X − P∥ ≤ 10τ, rounding X1 at 1/2 gives relative Hamming distance at most 4(10τ)2 from Ew. The exceptional top of the distinguished vertical is excluded from E and has field −e, where e = (0, 0, 0, 1). The initial choice of τ may impose any further fixed positive upper bounds, including validation and global-recovery radii. All these choices, and B1, c∗, β0, precede every numerical accuracy choice and the choice of a step size β.
